questions.solutionHtml:
Nitroprusside

questions.stem: A 59 year-old man with a long history of type 2 diabetes visits the clinic for a follow-up. He takes metformin, aspirin, and pravastatin. Besides diabetes, he was diagnosed with hypertension 1 year ago. He made lifestyle changes in the form of diet and exercise but they did not help in lowering his blood pressure. His BMI is 25 kg/m2 and his blood pressure today is 150/92 mmHg. What is the most appropriate treatment for this patient's hypertension?
questions.solutionHtml:
Losartan
  • Explanation:

    • ARBs provide renal protection and delay the progression to diabetic nephropathy. Though the effects of ACE inhibitors and ARBs are not identical, the latter has all the metabolic and prognostic advantages of ACE inhibitors.
  • Following are compelling indications for ARBs to be used for the treatment of hypertension:

    • Heart failure
    • Chronic kidney disease
    • Diabetes
    • Cad risk
    • Recurrent stroke prevention
  • Note:
    • Hydrochlorothiazide causes hyperglycemia
    • Metoprolol is not first-line antihypertensive
    • No need to continue lifestyle modi59-year-older next 3 months
